title: cli: the `pnpm dev` watcher prints only "✗ compile failed (Nms)" when a save is refused — the refusal goes to compile's stdout, which the watcher discards
body:
Filing gate: ① — a product defect with a named landing point and a reproduction.
Reader: central triage. Route it to the `packages/cli` lane, which owns `src/commands/dev.ts`. Found by the `repo:objectos` seat (objectstack-ai/objectstack#9831) during objectstack-ai/objectos#327 (PR objectstack-ai/objectos#336).
Dedupe: semantic search over objectstack for "dev watcher prints compile failed without the reason", "os dev compile failed no error message" and "dev server watch recompile spawn compile stdio ignore refusal not shown" → 0 relevant hits. The nearest hit is #12526, closed, about `serve-*` spawners. A positive control on the same search ("npm edgesOut vitest install crash") returns #23805/#23806, so the search reaches this repo.
reach: public door — `pnpm dev` on a fresh `os init my-app -t app` scaffold at `@objectstack/cli` 17.7.0, measured 2 of 2 boots.

## What happens

Save an object that the compile refuses, for example `name: 'task'` in a scaffold whose namespace is `my_app`. The dev server prints only:

```
  ↻ recompiling (src/objects/task.object.ts)...
  ✗ compile failed (2702ms)
```

The reason never appears. `pnpm build` on the same tree prints the refusal and exits 2:

```
✗ Object 'task' is missing the package namespace prefix. Rename it to 'my_app_task' (namespace = 'my_app')
```

## Why — `origin/main` `54770208`

`packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts:930-938` spawns `compile` with `stdio: opts.verbose ? 'inherit' : ['ignore', 'ignore', 'pipe']`, then prints `r.stderr` when the exit is non-zero. The refusal is written to **stdout**: the measured run produced 10 stdout lines including the refusal, and 0 stderr bytes. So the one message that says what to fix is discarded, unless the user knows to pass `--verbose`.

## Done looks like

On a non-zero compile exit, the watcher shows the refusal text — the lines `pnpm build` would print — without `--verbose`. A pin test proves it, using a fixture whose compile refusal is written to stdout.

The objectos quickstart currently works around this with "If it prints only `✗ compile failed`, run `pnpm build` to see why".
